unit.title: L'anglais académique
unit.goal: Écrire comme dans un rapport ou un essai : nuancer ses affirmations, rapporter une opinion de façon impersonnelle et transformer les verbes en noms.

lesson.text: Dans un essai, un rapport ou à l'examen Cambridge C2, on n'écrit pas « Tout le monde sait que les ados sont paresseux ! ». L'anglais académique est **prudent** (il nuance), **impersonnel** (il cache le « je » et le « on ») et **compact** (il adore les noms). Trois outils pour sonner comme une vraie chercheuse… même quand tu écris sur les chaussettes perdues.

lesson.title: Nuancer : le hedging
lesson.text: Pour éviter les affirmations trop absolues : [[It appears that…]] / [[It seems that…]] (il semble que) ; sujet + [[appears to]] / [[seems to]] + base verbale : [[The plan appears to work.]] ; [[tend to]] + base verbale (avoir tendance à) : [[Cats tend to sleep a lot.]] ; [[be likely to]] / [[be unlikely to]] + base verbale (il est probable / peu probable que) : [[Prices are likely to rise.]] ; l'adverbe [[arguably]] (on peut soutenir que, sans doute), placé devant ce qu'il nuance : [[This is arguably her best book.]] ; et [[to some extent]] (dans une certaine mesure). Les modaux [[may]], [[might]] et [[could]] nuancent aussi.

head: Trop absolu
Version académique
rows: [[Teenagers tend to sleep later than adults.]]
[[The bus is likely to be late.]]
[[This is arguably the best song of the decade.]]
[[To some extent, screens may affect our sleep.]]

lesson.title: Les structures impersonnelles
lesson.text: Pour rapporter une opinion générale sans dire qui la pense (le « on dit que » du français) : **1.** [[It is]] + participe passé + [[that]] : [[It is widely believed that…]], [[It is said that…]], [[It is thought that…]], [[It is expected that…]], [[It is known that…]]. **2.** Sujet + [[is]] + participe passé + [[to]] + base verbale : [[The castle is said to be haunted.]] (On dit que le château est hanté.) **3.** Pour un fait **passé**, [[to have]] + participe passé : [[The cake is thought to have disappeared during the night.]] (On pense que le gâteau a disparu pendant la nuit.) Variante avec [[there]] : [[There is said to be a tunnel under the school.]]

Pièges de francophone : **1.** « On dit que » ne se traduit pas par [[It is told that]] ✗ mais par [[It is said that]] ✓. **2.** Ne mélange pas les deux structures : [[He is believed that he is rich]] ✗ → [[He is believed to be rich]] ✓ ou [[It is believed that he is rich]] ✓. **3.** [[evidence]] (des preuves) et [[research]] (des recherches) sont **indénombrables** : jamais [[evidences]] ni [[researches]] ; on dit [[a piece of evidence]]. **4.** « Il est probable que Léa gagne » : [[Léa is likely to win]], jamais [[Léa is probable to win]] ✗. **5.** Après [[tend to]], [[appear to]] et [[be likely to]] : la **base verbale**, jamais -ing : [[tends to sleep]], pas [[tends to sleeping]].

lesson.title: La nominalisation
lesson.text: L'anglais académique transforme les verbes et les adjectifs en **noms** : la phrase devient plus compacte et plus objective. [[Prices rose quickly, which worried everyone.]] → [[The rapid rise in prices worried everyone.]] Remarque : l'adverbe ([[quickly]]) devient un **adjectif** ([[rapid]]), et le complément arrive avec [[of]] ou [[in]] : [[the introduction of a new rule]], [[a rise in prices]], [[the growth of the city]]. Le sujet peut devenir un possessif : [[The mayor decided…]] → [[The mayor's decision…]]

head: Verbe / adjectif
Nom
Exemple
rows: [[The failure of the plan was obvious.]]

items.en: It appears that the printer has run out of ink.
items.fr: Il semble que l'imprimante n'ait plus d'encre.

items.en: Raccoons tend to visit our garbage bins on Tuesday nights.
items.fr: Les ratons laveurs ont tendance à visiter nos poubelles le mardi soir.

items.en: It is widely believed that cats always land on their feet.
items.fr: Beaucoup croient que les chats retombent toujours sur leurs pattes.

items.en: The painting is thought to have been hidden in the attic for decades.
items.fr: On pense que le tableau a été caché dans le grenier pendant des décennies.

items.en: The arrival of the new puppy changed our routine completely.
items.fr: L'arrivée du nouveau chiot a complètement changé notre routine.

items.en: Hockey is arguably the most popular sport in Canada.
items.fr: Le hockey est sans doute le sport le plus populaire au Canada.

lines.en: Dad, can you read my science report? My teacher says it sounds too casual.
lines.fr: Papa, peux-tu lire mon rapport de sciences ? Mon enseignante dit qu'il sonne trop familier.

lines.en: Let's see. "Everybody knows that dogs are smarter than cats." Hmm, that's a bit strong.
lines.fr: Voyons. « Tout le monde sait que les chiens sont plus intelligents que les chats. » Hum, c'est un peu fort.

lines.en: Fine. "It is widely believed that dogs are smarter than cats." Better?
lines.fr: D'accord. « Beaucoup pensent que les chiens sont plus intelligents que les chats. » C'est mieux ?

lines.en: Much better. And what about "Our cat is lazy"?
lines.fr: Beaucoup mieux. Et « Notre chat est paresseux » ?

lines.en: "Our cat tends to spend most of the day asleep."
lines.fr: « Notre chat a tendance à passer la plus grande partie de la journée à dormir. »

lines.en: "Further research is needed. Arguably, the cat is the smartest member of this family."
lines.fr: « D'autres recherches sont nécessaires. On peut soutenir que le chat est le membre le plus intelligent de cette famille. »

lines.en: That appears to be true, but let's not tell your mother.
lines.fr: Ça semble vrai, mais n'en parlons pas à ta mère.

lesson.text: Le sais-tu ? Pendant la Seconde Guerre mondiale, les Britanniques ont fait circuler l'idée que leurs pilotes voyaient la nuit grâce aux carottes. Selon une explication souvent avancée, c'était pour cacher une nouvelle technologie : le radar. Résultat : [[it is still widely believed that carrots help you see in the dark]]. Elles contiennent bien de quoi fabriquer de la vitamine A, utile aux yeux, mais elles ne donnent pas une vision de chat ! Remarque comme cette anecdote est **nuancée** (« selon une explication souvent avancée », en anglais [[it is often said that]]) : c'est du hedging !

vocab.fr: on peut soutenir que, sans doute
vocab.ex: This is arguably the best poutine in Gatineau.
It appears that the meeting has been cancelled.
Cats tend to sleep during the day.

vocab.fr: être probable que, risquer de (+ base verbale)
vocab.ex: The roads are likely to be icy tomorrow morning.
It is widely believed that lightning never strikes the same place twice.

vocab.fr: on pense que… (X is thought to…)
vocab.ex: The ring is thought to be very old.

vocab.fr: on dit que… (X is said to…)
vocab.ex: The lake is said to be bottomless.
To some extent, the weather affected the results.
There is no evidence that the dog ate my homework.
The findings of the study surprised the scientists.
More research is needed on this question.
There has been a significant increase in visitors this year.
The growth of the city has been very fast.
The failure of the experiment taught us a lot.
The likelihood of snow tonight is very high.
Our first assumption turned out to be wrong.
Some people claim that they have seen a ghost.
There has been a decline in the number of bees.

sentences.en: It is widely believed that breakfast is the most important meal of the day.
sentences.fr: Il est communément admis que le déjeuner (petit-déjeuner) est le repas le plus important de la journée.

sentences.en: The old house is thought to have been built over two centuries ago.
sentences.fr: On pense que la vieille maison a été construite il y a plus de deux siècles.

sentences.en: Teenagers tend to go to bed later than their parents.
sentences.fr: Les ados ont tendance à se coucher plus tard que leurs parents.

sentences.en: Our neighbour's dog is likely to bark when the mail carrier arrives.
sentences.fr: Le chien de notre voisin va sans doute japper quand le facteur arrivera.

sentences.en: It appears that someone has eaten the last piece of cake.
sentences.fr: Il semble que quelqu'un ait mangé le dernier morceau de gâteau.

sentences.en: There is no evidence that the house is haunted.
sentences.fr: Il n'y a aucune preuve que la maison soit hantée.

sentences.en: This is arguably the best poutine in the whole city.
sentences.fr: C'est sans doute la meilleure poutine de toute la ville.
alt: Arguably, this is the best poutine in the whole city.

sentences.en: The introduction of longer recess was a great success.
sentences.fr: L'introduction d'une récréation plus longue a été un grand succès.

sentences.en: The rapid growth of the city has caused serious traffic problems.
sentences.fr: La croissance rapide de la ville a causé de graves problèmes de circulation.

sentences.en: Her refusal to answer the question surprised the whole class.
sentences.fr: Son refus de répondre à la question a surpris toute la classe.

sentences.en: The findings of our class survey were rather surprising.
sentences.fr: Les résultats du sondage de notre classe étaient plutôt surprenants.

sentences.en: Moose are said to be excellent swimmers.
sentences.fr: On dit que les orignaux sont d'excellents nageurs.

grammar.q: The new bridge ___ to open next spring.
grammar.explain: On veut dire « on s'attend à ce que le pont ouvre » : sujet + is expected + to. Le pont, lui, n'attend rien du tout !

grammar.q: Quelle phrase convient le mieux à un rapport académique ?
choices: Everybody knows that kids hate vegetables.
Kids totally hate vegetables, for sure.
Children tend to prefer sweet foods to vegetables.
Kids hate vegetables, end of story.
grammar.explain: Tend to nuance l'affirmation, et children est plus neutre que kids. Les autres phrases sont trop absolues et trop familières.

grammar.q: The storm is thought ___ a lot of damage last night.
grammar.explain: La tempête a eu lieu hier soir (fait passé) : is thought + to have + participe passé.

grammar.q: Quel nom correspond au verbe « arrive » ?
grammar.explain: Arrive → arrival, comme refuse → refusal. Arrivation et arrivance n'existent pas.

grammar.q: This is ___ the funniest movie the director has ever made.
grammar.explain: Il faut un adverbe pour nuancer le superlatif : arguably (on peut soutenir que). Arguable est un adjectif.

grammar.q: There ___ to be a secret tunnel under the old school.
grammar.explain: « On dit qu'il y a… » = There is said to be… On ne dit jamais is told dans ce sens.

grammar.q: Our dog ___ to bark at anyone wearing a hat.
grammar.explain: Our dog = it : tend prend un -s, puis to + base verbale (bark).

grammar.q: It is widely ___ that the early bird catches the worm.
grammar.explain: Structure impersonnelle : It is + participe passé + that. Believe → believed.

grammar.lead: People say that the old lighthouse is haunted.
grammar.explain: Sujet + is said + to + base verbale : The lighthouse is said to be haunted.

grammar.lead: People think that the thief escaped through the window.
grammar.explain: La fuite est passée : is thought + to have + participe passé (escaped).

grammar.lead: Because the team failed, the coach was furious.
grammar.q: The team's ___ made the coach furious.
grammar.explain: Nominalisation : le verbe fail devient le nom failure (l'échec).

grammar.q: Maya ___ win the race: she has trained all summer.
grammar.explain: Be likely to + base verbale = il est probable que. Maya = she, donc is.

grammar.q: The city has seen rapid ___ over the last ten years.
grammar.explain: Après l'adjectif rapid, il faut un nom : grow → growth (la croissance).

grammar.q: There is not enough evidences to prove that he cheated.
grammar.explain: Evidence est indénombrable : jamais de -s. Pour une seule preuve : a piece of evidence.

grammar.q: The ship is believed to have sank in a storm.
grammar.explain: Après to have, il faut le participe passé : sink, sank, sunk.

grammar.q: My little brother tends to asking the same question ten times.
grammar.explain: Tend to + base verbale : tends to ask, jamais -ing.

grammar.q: It is widely belief that goldfish have a very short memory.
grammar.explain: Il faut le participe passé du verbe : It is widely believed that… Belief est le nom (la croyance).

grammar.q: The decide to cancel the trip disappointed everyone.
grammar.explain: Après The, il faut un nom : decide → decision.

reading.title: The Case of the Missing Socks
reading.text:
For generations, it has been widely believed that washing machines eat socks. In most homes, the disappearance of single socks tends to be blamed on the dryer, the cat or a younger brother. However, there appears to be very little evidence for any of these claims. This report presents the findings of a small investigation carried out in my own home over a period of six weeks.

The research began with a simple assumption: socks do not simply vanish. Every sock that entered the laundry room was counted before and after each wash. The results were significant. During the investigation, eleven socks went missing, but nine of them were eventually found: four under beds, three in the sleeves of sweaters, one inside a duvet cover and one in the dog's basket.

It is therefore unlikely that the washing machine is responsible. The dog, on the other hand, is thought to have stolen at least one sock, although he has refused to comment. Arguably, the real problem is not the machine but human behaviour: socks tend to be dropped, kicked under furniture or forgotten in sports bags.

Of course, this study has its limits. Only one family took part, and the likelihood of errors in counting is fairly high, especially when the person counting is a teenager who is easily distracted by video games. To some extent, the results may also have been affected by the fact that everyone knew about the investigation and was more careful than usual.

Nevertheless, the findings suggest that the growth of the famous "sock monster" legend is mainly due to our own carelessness. Further research is needed. In the meantime, two missing socks are still believed to be somewhere in the house.

questions.q: What was the starting point of the investigation?
choices: The belief that washing machines eat socks
The idea that socks do not simply disappear
A complaint from the writer's younger brother
A science fair organized by the school

questions.q: Where were most of the missing socks found?
According to the report, what is the main cause of missing socks?
Why does the writer say that the dog "has refused to comment"?
choices: Because the dog was sleeping during the interview
Because the writer is having fun with a serious academic style
Because the dog is afraid of the washing machine
Because the family decided not to ask the dog

questions.q: Which limit of the study does the writer mention?
choices: The washing machine was too old.
The study lasted only one week.
The family did not count the socks.

questions.q: What can we infer about the writer of the report?
choices: He or she is a teenager in the family.
He or she is a professional scientist.
He or she sells washing machines.
He or she lives alone with a dog.

pron.focus: Les mots en -ate : verbe ou nom ?
pron.explain: L'anglais académique adore les mots en [[-ate]], et beaucoup sont à la fois **verbe** et **nom** ou **adjectif**. L'orthographe ne change pas, mais le son, oui ! Quand c'est un **verbe**, la fin est pleine : « éït » ([[to estimate]], [[to separate]]). Quand c'est un **nom** ou un **adjectif**, la fin devient un petit « eut » tout faible ([[an estimate]], [[separate rooms]]). L'accent, lui, reste au début. Honnêtement, la voix de synthèse se trompe parfois : fie-toi à la règle et à ton oreille.

words.hint: « tou-ESS-ti-méït » : verbe, la fin sonne « éït »
« eun-ESS-ti-meut » : nom, la fin est un petit « eut »
« eu-PROK-si-meut-li » : adverbe, le « ate » devient « meut »

practice: We estimate that the estimate is approximately right.
Please separate the papers into two separate piles.
My sister will graduate in June, and then she will be a graduate!

mission.prompt: Ton club de sciences a fait un sondage sur le sommeil des élèves de ton école. Écris le paragraphe de conclusion du rapport (cinq à huit phrases) dans un style académique : au moins deux outils de nuance, une structure impersonnelle et deux nominalisations.
mission.model: It is widely believed that teenagers do not get enough sleep, and our survey of sixty students appears to confirm this assumption. Most students tend to go to bed after eleven o'clock on school nights. A significant number also admitted that they check their phones in bed. Screens are thought to delay the production of the hormone that helps us fall asleep. Arguably, the introduction of a later start time would improve concentration in class. However, further research is needed before any firm recommendation can be made.
checklist: J'ai nuancé avec au moins deux outils : [[tend to]], [[appears to]], [[is likely to]], [[arguably]]…
J'ai utilisé une structure impersonnelle : [[It is widely believed that…]] ou [[X is thought to…]]
Après [[is thought to]] ou [[tends to]], j'ai mis la base verbale
J'ai transformé au moins deux verbes en noms ([[the introduction of]], [[the production of]])
J'ai évité les affirmations absolues comme [[everybody knows]]
